The Hill We Promised

Spec short film. 5-7 minutes, silent-heavy love story for a film festival and an Instagram Reels series. My role: story, screenplay, minimalist dialogue and scene breakdown.

Ten years later.

He promised to wait 10 years on a hill. She came to check if he did. He was already there, soaked in rain.

  • The Hill We Promised
  • Ten Years Later
  • Promise Station

Logline

When a girl challenges a boy's love proposal to prove itself after ten years, she gives him only a place and a promise: a hill. A decade later, she returns not to meet him, but to secretly see if he kept his word.

The opening scene

A noisy school ground. A teenage boy proposes.

She: This is infatuation, not love.

He: It's love.

She smiles.

She: If you still feel the same after 10 years, meet me at my favourite hill. If you come, I will love you at any cost. That's my promise station.

He: Okay.

He says it like it's easy. Cut to ten years later.

Structure

  1. Then, 30 secondsYoung, impulsive love meets a mature challenge. The promise is made casually, but shot like a sacred vow.
  2. Now, 2 minutesShe has changed: more guarded, more real. She goes to the hill but hides at a distance, just to check. Will he really come?
  3. The reveal, 2 minutesThe camera slowly shows he is already there, soaked in rain, with no umbrella and no phone. He came early and has been waiting. Love wasn't infatuation. It was patience.
  4. Ending, 30 secondsNo dialogue. She steps out into the rain. He looks up. Ten years ends in one look.

Tone and visuals

Minimal dialogue, maximum emotion. Natural light, a misty hilltop and grey rain, with one red umbrella (hers) against him drenched. It's about showing love, not saying it.

Core theme

Love is not about how intensely you feel in a moment, but how quietly you wait for years.

The Girl Who Wasn't a Fan

Spec short film or web-series pilot. Romance and family drama. My role: story, screenplay and scene breakdown. Structure and sample lines below are my first draft, ready to refine.

  • The Girl Who Wasn't a Fan
  • The Boy She Forgot
  • Still Remembered

Millions know his name. The one girl he came back for doesn't remember it.

Logline

A famous sportsman adored by millions returns to marry his childhood love, but she has no memory of him. Her possessive sister, his biggest fan, wants the spotlight he gives only to her. When their parents, who still remember him and stay in touch with his family, suggest the marriage, she must decide whether to trust a stranger whose fame she doesn't care about.

Structure

  1. The suggestionHer parents bring up the marriage over dinner. They remember the boy and have never lost touch with his parents. She remembers nothing. Her sister drops her fork.
  2. The fan sisterThe sister has his poster, his jersey and every match saved. She is possessive of him and of her sister's attention, and her sweetness turns sharp when the spotlight moves. The heroine already finds her character hard to bear.
  3. The forgottenHe doesn't use fame to win her. He remembers small things from childhood and lets them return to her one at a time. She doesn't remember, but she notices that he never asks her to.
  4. The choiceThe sister's jealousy peaks in public. The heroine chooses on her own terms, not for the crowd, her sister or her parents.

Tone and visuals

Warm family rooms against loud stadium noise. The crowd is always heard, never trusted. Intimate scenes are quiet and close.

Core theme

Being loved by millions is not the same as being known by one.

4 AM

4:00 AM

Short first-person story, under 100 words. Playful, light and romantic.

I wake up at 4 AM every day to get ready for my sports practice. Three days ago, I saw a girl on my neighbour's balcony as I was leaving. I don't know who she is, and she had never seen me before.

Today, I stood near my gate and watched her. She was trying to look at me too, and when she noticed I was looking at her, then guess what happened, guys: she blushed.

I am being delulu too.
